title: A browser test
summary: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server.
introduction: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Run these TypeScript test files in a local Playwright project. The site only displays them; its normal JavaScript playground is not a browser-test runner.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Playwright. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.title: A browser test

blocks.text: The test finds a visible heading named Library.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the heading and the expected name.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Install Playwright and its browser with the official setup guide before running a test file.
For more detail later, use this [Playwright further reading](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro).

seo.title: Playwright: A browser test
seo.description: Learn about a browser test in Playwright. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
